label: Filesystem requests and responses preserve request_id; file chunks expose index, totals, checksum, and is_last; typed errors distinguish retryable rate limits from terminal failures.
Filesystem access layers absolute-path and symlink checks, canonical jail enforcement, denied/read-only globs, size/result caps, per-socket token-bucket limits, and retry_after_ms.
Push tokens require auth and a push scope, replace per installation, deduplicate exact values, cap at three per credential, and are pruned when credentials become inactive.

Waiting push delivery is spawned separately from websocket broadcast and carries session identifiers plus waiting_for_input, but sender construction currently filters to Expo tokens despite accepting APNs and FCM registrations.
Filesystem retries preserve request identity and treat retry_after_ms as actionable server backoff, while permission and validation errors are terminal until user intent or configuration changes.
Push delivery must remain independent of the authoritative websocket stream and must be keyed to active credential/install registrations.
CopyPath is write-scoped and rate-limited but bypasses the destructive-operation flag used by delete and rename.
The registered push-token type set is broader than the currently implemented Expo send path.

direction: Treat push delivery as part of websocket stream correctness
reason: The daemon explicitly broadcasts waiting state and performs push I/O in a separate spawned task.
